confirmed: Read the entire local markdown, including references and Appendix A, and checked the relevant PDF pages. The PDF has 17 pages and is labeled arXiv:2302.12832v2 [cs.CL], 2 Jun 2023; source.version and source.pages are correct (PDF p. 1, arXiv stamp and ACM reference; p. 17, Appendix A).

The three study entries are correctly distinguished: model-only prompt engineering, a human problem-reformulation study, and a model-output harmfulness audit; this is not a synthesis or an AI-versus-human output comparison (PDF pp. 3-6, Sections 3.1-3.3; pp. 6-10, Section 4; p. 11, Section 5).

The human study first required unassisted initial formulation/ideation, followed by two analogy-assisted phases for everyone. Random assignment concerned analogy sets; all human-study analogies came from the same one-shot Duncker run. No randomized AI-access contrast, randomized AI-configuration contrast, or randomized no-AI/AI order is reported, supporting quasi_people, observational context, core=no, and has_randomized_people_study=false (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.3; p. 13, Section 6.2.1; p. 17, Figures A1-A2).

The human sample was 123 enrolled, 13 excluded for not finishing the second round, and 110 analyzed completers; the task lasted 30 mins. Both phase arms describe the same 110 people, so they must not be added together. The analyzed sample exceeds 50, and enrollment is not a reported count randomized between assistance conditions (PDF p. 8, Section 4.1.3; p. 9, Section 4.2).

All three reported strings match the PDF exactly: adding 185/220 (84.09%), rejecting 23/220 (10.45%), and both adding and rejecting 22/220 (10%). The joint category overlaps the other categories, and these are descriptive response frequencies rather than randomized treatment effects (PDF p. 10, Table 2, recovered with find_tables(), and Section 4.2.2).

The one_line_finding correctly states 110 completers, 185/220 additions (84.09%), and 23/220 rejections (10.45%), without a randomized comparison of assistance (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 4.1.2-4.1.3; p. 10, Table 2).

The human outcomes are expert-coded properties of produced reformulation responses: adding is elaboration, and rejecting/shifting are other output-based reformulation measures. The study does not report overall creativity, novelty, usefulness ratings of human solutions, or across-person output diversity; participants instead rated the helpfulness of the supplied analogies. This supports the form’s stated limitation on criterion 3 and its separation of output coding from subjective helpfulness (PDF pp. 8-10, Sections 4.1.2, 4.1.4, and 4.2).

The model was GPT-3 text-davinci-002. Prompt engineering generated 480 problem-analogy pairs across six design problems with zero-shot, two one-shot runs, and a few-shot prompt containing three examples; a single blinded PhD-level researcher evaluated the generated analogies. These counts describe model outputs and an evaluator, not randomized creative-task participants (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1-3.2).

The human task used 108 selected unique analogies from the one-shot Duncker run; the harmfulness audit reviewed the same 108 analogies. These are stimulus counts, not additional human participants (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.1.1; p. 11, Section 5.1).

Separate Supplementary Material is cited for generation code/analogies and completed participants’ analogy-response pairs. The included Appendix A contains task screenshots rather than that data/code supplement; despite its Study 2 heading, the methods identify these as Study 1 interfaces (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 8, Section 4.1.2; p. 9, Section 4.2; p. 17, Appendix A).
Synthesis fields correctly remain at their defaults: no meta-analysis, pooled estimate, interval, or standardization is reported for these original empirical studies (PDF Sections 3-5, pp. 3-12).
summary: The nonrandomized observational classification, 110 analyzed participants, source version, and all reported reformulation frequencies are supported; no qualifying randomized people study was found. Seven corrections address the corrupted title and missing output counts, exclusions, country, coding details, AI availability, and timing.
